newsitem.title: USA: PACCAR net falls after takeover.
newsitem.headline: PACCAR net falls after takeover.

text.p: Paccar Inc., maker of Kenworth, Peterbilt and Foden heavy-duty trucks, said Tuesday its profits fell in the fourth quarter after it paid $543.8 million for European truck manufacturer DAF Trucks N.V. in November.
But the lower results did not hurt its stock, which surged $5.875 to $73.375 on Nasdaq in late morning trading.
Paccar's earnings slid to $62.5 million, or $1.61 per share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $65.1 million, or $1.67 per share, a year earlier.
As a result of the takeover, sales edged up to $1.2 billion from $1.1 billion.
Full-year 1996 net income fell to $201.0 million, or $5.17 per share, from $252.8 million, or $6.50 per share, in 1995. Sales dropped to $4.3 billion from $4.6 billion.

"Last year was a strong year for heavy-duty truck manufacturing -- much better, in fact, than many in the industry anticipated," said Mark Pigott, chairman and chief executive. "Paccar increased its market share (of the largest trucks) as more trucking companies specified our products."
Pigott said analysts expect 1997 to be a reasonable year for truck manufacturers despite softer markets in both North America and Europe.

Paccar, which also provides financial services, said profits surged in this business as its overall portfolio in finance and leasing grew. The Bellevue, Wash.-based company's Mexican finance subsidiary required significantly lower credit loss provisions in 1996.
